subject.title: [Feature Request]: Multi-lane concurrency support for sub-agents via sessions_spawn

question: Should `sessions_spawn` accept only administrator-configured lane names with both per-lane and aggregate limits, or may agents create arbitrary dynamic lanes?
rationale: Without a trusted namespace and aggregate budget, caller-selected lanes can evade the existing global resource guard; the correct configuration and fallback contract requires maintainer intent.

options.title: Configured lanes plus aggregate cap
options.body: Allow only declared lane profiles, preserve `subagent` as the default, and enforce both each lane's limit and a total sub-agent limit.

options.title: Dynamic caller-created lanes
options.body: Allow arbitrary lane names and accept the larger resource-governance, validation, and configuration-growth surface.

options.title: Keep one spawn lane
options.body: Retain the global subagent lane and address isolation through per-agent limits, priorities, or queue visibility instead.

recommendation.title: Configured lanes plus aggregate cap
recommendation.body: Allow only declared lane profiles, preserve `subagent` as the default, and enforce both each lane's limit and a total sub-agent limit.

likelyOwner.reason: The implementation history and direct issue participation connect this person most closely to the existing `sessions_spawn` concurrency contract.
